answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the BMX park read as a sunny stylized dirt-jump park, or grimy urban concrete?
answers.answer: Make it a sunny stylized dirt-jump park; that is the simplest, clearest fit for the BMX gameplay.

answers.ask: Does the BMX section end at a finish line you race to, or is it a freestyle area you ride around?
answers.answer: Use a finish line the player races to after completing the obby and building speed.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D BMX game map as a sunny, stylized dirt-jump park. A compact obstacle-course section leads into a BMX run, with a clear route toward a finish line after the obby; arrange dirt ramps and jumps along the racing path.
agent_notes: The sentence is about a BMX game and the answer put a finish line at the end of it, which is Racing's finish condition rather than Obby's own-pace climb, so Racing leads and Obby & Platformer is named second for the speed-earning obstacle section. I considered the Simulation stat-grind reading, since speed is a number you build, but there are no gated tiers, no shop and no rebirth here — the speed is spent on one race, so the race is the game. route-point-to-point is the default and the right one: obby section into a sprint that starts in one place and ends at the finish, with no laps to make it a circuit. Obstacle Race fits as the preset, and I added path-road-vehicle so the course builds as a continuous ridable surface rather than discrete jump platforms — a bike needs roadway — plus obstacle-jump for the dirt jumps and powerup-buffs to carry the speed the obby awards. Without a user I read hazard-kill as the fall-away edges of the dirt-jump park rather than lethal traps, and kept the whole thing on the genre-wide P6, which is proven and must not be dropped.
